1 فَطَسَ , (S, M, A, Msb, K,) aor.
فَطِسَ (S, Msb, K) and
فَطُسَ , (Msb,) inf. n. فُطُوسٌ, (S, M, &c.,) He died; (S, M, &c.;) as also طَفَسَ: (TA:) or he died without disease: (M:) or without any apparent disease. (TA.) ＝
-A2- فَطَسَ الحَدِيدَ, (A, O, K, TA,) aor.
فَطِسَ , (K, * TA,) inf. n. فَطْسٌ, (TA,) He made the iron broad (A, O, K) with the great hammer called فِطِّيس: (A:) or he beat the iron. (TA.) ―
-b2- And الفَطْسُ signifies The treading vehemently, or the compressing vehemently. (M, TA: the word thus doubly rendered is الوَطْءُ.) ―
-b3- And you say, فَطَسْتُهُ عَنْ كَذَا meaning I repelled him in a most evil manner from such a thing: and likewise I beat him [app. away from such a thing]. (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K.) ―
-b4- And فَطَسَهُ بِالكَلِمَةِ, (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K,) and بِالخَبَرِ, (Ibn- 'Abbád, O,) aor.
فَطِسَ , (K,) He uttered in his face [the word, or sentence, and the tidings, or information]; as also ↓ فطّسهُ , (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K,) inf. n. تَفْطِيسٌ. (Ibn-'Abbád, O.) ＝
-A3- فِطِسَ, aor.
فَطَسَ , inf. n. فَطَسٌ, (S, M, A, K,) He had the bone of his nose wide and depressed; (M;) or depressed and expanded: (S, A, K:) he had his nose spreading upon his face. (A, K.) [And فَطِئَ app. signifies the same.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
